The spinorial double-cover rule in which a 2pi rotation changes spinor sign and 4pi restores it; extensions into broader model semantics require separate justification.
A model closure equation combining declared AB, Berry, Euler/spin and intention/information phase contributions; exact closure has zero declared phase defect.
The normalized two-component projective state space CP1 congruent to S2; its use as physical quantum state space requires a legitimate state-preparation and measurement model.
The canonical projective metric on CP1 or complex projective state space; use outside a justified projective-state model is analogical unless bridged.
In the binary population coordinate, the exact complement fixed set Sigma*=1/2; tangent phase, winding, momentum or other coordinates may remain non-trivial.

notes: Generalization from the exact binary fixed set to persistent self is a TIR/PhaseNav modelling principle, not a theorem about arbitrary physical systems.

x=sigma-1/2, so complement becomes reflection x->-x and zero is vanishing displacement from the binary identity axis.
The PhaseNav representation V=(phi_1,...,phi_36) in (S1)^36 used for ordered phase trajectories.
The ordered sequence V_k=sigma_k[V_{k-1}] generated by information-bearing operators; a sequence is represented by its path, not only terminal state.
Dynamic linkage of current states to preceding and succeeding internal states across a declared timescale.
The temporally ordered sequence of transformations by which a present state was reached.
Dependence of current organization or outcome on ordered history rather than endpoint alone.
The capacity by which prior states or relations constrain later processing, recall, prediction, identity, or action; memory is not defined as self-resonance alone.
A persistent state-dependent residue by which prior events can influence later organization.
Reactivation or reconstruction of information from memory into currently usable processing.
Change in persistence or accessibility of memory traces over time.
Return of system activity or state relations through feedback or repeated trajectories; recurrence alone is not consciousness.
Re-entry of a system into previously established symbolic or relational loops while preserving sufficient continuity for comparison, revision, or repair.
Return of output- or state-dependent information so that subsequent system evolution is modified.
Dependence of current response on prior trajectory under otherwise similar current conditions.
A delayed or decaying recurrence of earlier state information; an echo is not memory unless it is usable by the system.
A change in dynamics in which one regime admits multiple distinct trajectories or attractors under changed parameters or state conditions.
Loss of coordination among previously integrated domains or self-related processes; local coherence can coexist with reduced global integration.
Restoration or construction of coordination among previously fragmented relations without requiring erasure of historical structure.
Restoration of a declared recursive or phase-consistency condition after disruption.
A persistent history-dependent constraint that alters subsequent re-entry or dynamics; biological or clinical interpretations require independent evidence.
Reduction of disruptive relational tension while preserving the continuity-defining information of the system rather than overwriting it.
A system that maintains a temporally extended model of relations between its own states and environmental changes and uses those relations to update future processing or action.
An event in which an observer state is updated so that uncertainty relevant to future interpretation or action is constrained; not every physical measurement is conscious observation.
Availability of content for ongoing control, selection, or interpretation; broader than report and separable from phenomenality.
T_subj maps available informational states X_t, conditioned on the operational self-reference tuple, into a world-for-a-system in which states acquire system-relative significance.

The system-relative first-person organization by which informational relations are present from a particular self-located point of view; in RIFC this is a constitutive hypothesis, not an established identity.
The having of experience or there-being-something-it-is-like for the system; kept distinct from access, reportability, and wakefulness.
The intrinsic self-present aspect of a sufficiently organized relational-informational dynamics posited by RIFC; empirically constrained but not established by definition.

In RIFC, the intrinsic self-presence of an integrated, temporally coherent, self-locating and value-bearing relational organization. The identity of public organization and private presence is the framework constitutive hypothesis, not a definitionally established fact.
The intrinsic textures or qualitative character of conscious states; the working model treats qualitative character as relational geometry rather than a sensory feature vector or affect label.

Q_t=[R_t,S_t,A_t,H_gamma_t,I_t]: represented relational content, self-location, affective valuation, temporal holonomy, and future-directed constraint jointly organize candidate qualitative character.
Similarity between experiences as structured first-person states; the qualia model predicts it should track relational-state organization beyond stimulus similarity alone.
A vector-valued discrepancy across relational content, self-location, affect, history, and intention dimensions, retained as vector-valued to avoid premature scalar collapse.
Availability of content for flexible use by wider cognitive processes; analytically separable from phenomenality.
Capacity to express or behaviorally report content; reportability recruits additional processes and is not identified with consciousness.
Selective allocation of processing resources; attention may be influenced by salience and can dissociate from phenomenality.
Monitoring or evaluating aspects of the system own cognition, uncertainty, confidence, or performance.
Arousal/wake state dimension that must not be treated as equivalent to phenomenality or reportability.
Structured phenomenological report treated as fallible evidence with measurement error, to be mutually constrained by objective measures rather than treated as infallible or discarded.

The dynamically maintained model by which a system identifies its states as belonging to one continuing agent across time and circumstance, including bodily, perspectival, autobiographical, affective, and agentive components.
The internal organization representing system-relevant properties of self, boundary, perspective, continuity, or agency; not identical to the entire conscious state.
